name: sqlparse
input_api: sqlparse.parse(local SQL text) -> tuple of grouped Statement token trees
scope: One SQL statement from local text; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Non-validating: it groups tokens into a tree and accepts invalid SQL, so it does not reject non-SQL input.
family: sqlparse regex lexer and token-grouping engine (non-validating)
family_note: sqlparse.parse lexes with the regex tables in sqlparse/keywords.py and sqlparse/lexer.py, then sqlparse/engine/grouping.py groups tokens into Identifier, IdentifierList, Function, Where, Comparison, Parenthesis and Values nodes under a Statement. The INSERT target 'orders (id, ...)' is grouped as a Function-shaped node; the adapter reads its name and parenthesized identifier list. Independent of sqlglot, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs. sql-metadata wraps this family.

popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads include Django's dependency on sqlparse for SQL formatting and splitting, not only parse-tree use.

name: sqlglot
input_api: sqlglot.parse(local SQL text, read=None) -> list of Expression trees
scope: One SQL statement from local text with the default dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. The optional sqlglotc and sqlglotrs accelerators are absent; other dialects are untested.
family: sqlglot pure-Python tokenizer and recursive-descent parser
family_note: sqlglot.parse tokenizes with sqlglot/tokens.py and tokenizer_core.py and parses with sqlglot/parser.py into exp.Expression nodes. The adapter reads exp.Select/exp.Insert arguments and walks exp.Table, exp.Func (excluding AND/OR connectors and operators) and exp.Literal nodes. Independent of sqlparse, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs. sqlglotrs (an optional Rust tokenizer) and sqlglotc are accelerators of this family, not separate parsers.

name: sqlfluff
input_api: sqlfluff.parse(local SQL text, dialect="ansi") -> parse-tree record
scope: One SQL statement from local text with the ansi dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Linting, fixing, other dialects and the optional sqlfluffrs extra are untested.
family: sqlfluff lexer and dialect grammar matcher
family_note: sqlfluff is a linter, but sqlfluff.parse is a documented parse API: it lexes with core/parser/lexer.py and matches the ansi dialect's segment grammar (dialects/dialect_ansi.py, core/parser/grammar) into a full parse tree, returned as nested {segment_type: value} records. It fails with APIParsingError on unparsable input. The adapter walks select_statement, select_clause_element, join_clause, where_clause, groupby_clause, orderby_clause, function_name_identifier, table_reference, insert_statement, values_clause, quoted_literal and numeric_literal segments. Independent of sqlparse, sqlglot, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs; sqlfluffrs (an optional Rust lexer) is an accelerator of this family and is not installed.

name: pglast
license_evidence: pyproject.toml license = "GPL-3.0-or-later" and source headers in the pinned sdist (no separate license file is shipped); the vendored libpg_query LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause (SHA-256 f9352c20940619a380a5e9f23cebe34d8f797cfbd747fc236a7a3e5fc8ef9b41)
input_api: pglast.parse_sql(local SQL text) -> tuple of pglast.ast.RawStmt nodes
scope: One SQL statement from local text with the PostgreSQL 18 grammar; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Source-built with LLVM coverage instead of the optimised wheel; the prettifier and the JSON/protobuf variants are untested.
family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
family_note: pglast vendors libpg_query 18.1.0 (the same release as the C libpg_query path) and links it statically. parse_sql calls pg_query_raw_parse and converts the C node tree into pglast.ast objects in its own Cython layer (pglast/parser.c from parser.pyx and ast.pyx); it does not go through libpg_query's JSON or protobuf output. The adapter reads SelectStmt (targetList, fromClause, whereClause, groupClause, sortClause), InsertStmt (relation, cols, selectStmt.valuesLists), RangeVar, JoinExpr, FuncCall and A_Const nodes. Its vendored libpg_query/src tree equals the 18.1.0 release tag used by the C path except pg_query_json_plpgsql.c, the C++ protobuf output file and the PostgreSQL COPYRIGHT file, so the grammar, scanner and raw_parser sources are byte-identical; pglast's own differential is its Cython conversion layer (pglast/parser.c: 735 select-only and 161 insert-only AFL++ features). A distinct package API over the shared libpg_query family; pg_query 0.29 is its predecessor PyPI name and is not a separate path.

name: sqloxide
license_evidence: LICENSE in the pinned sdist (SHA-256 4887ed0505457d387e7f7effda202be2374379f4fecf491e54ca67f59a77640b); the compiled-in sqlparser 0.61.0 crate is Apache-2.0
input_api: sqloxide.parse_sql(local SQL text, dialect="generic") -> list of statement ASTs (Python dicts)
scope: One SQL statement from local text with the generic dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Source-built with Rust coverage instead of the optimised wheel; restore_ast, the visitors and other dialects are untested.
family_note: sqloxide is a pyo3 binding: parse_sql maps the dialect name with sqlparser's dialect_from_str, calls sqlparser 0.61.0 Parser::parse_sql and converts the AST to Python objects with pythonize. The tokenizer and parser that produce the tree are sqlparser-rs, shared with the Rust sqlparser path (0.64.0); this is a distinct Python package API over that family, and its parser feedback is sqlparser-rs code. The adapter reads Query/Select (projection, from with joins, selection, group_by), order_by, Function, Table, Value and Insert/Values nodes.
